newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thinly-traded German shares start week tentatively.
newsitem.headline: Thinly-traded German shares start week tentatively.

text.p: German shares got off to a tentative start on Monday, dipping slightly in early bourse dealings on profit-taking after last week's record highs and keeping an eye out for U.S. data due in the afternoon.
The 30-share blue chip DAX index was down 9.34 points, or 0.35 percent, at 2,649.70 points while the December DAX futures contract was down 10 points at 2,667.5.

Dealers attributed the decline to a mild bout of profit-taking after the DAX surged to new records last week but said the vast majority of investors were holding back from the market amid a dearth of strong corporate news.
"The one positive we have is the dollar, which is looking very firm," said one dealer. "But buying interest is a flat zero at the moment."
U.S. data due this afternoon, including new home sales and the Chicago Purchasing Managers' Index, could help to inject some life into the market, dealers predicted.

Among individual stocks, chemical group BASF AG extended its losses from Friday, when it fell on news that a U.S. advisory committee had recommending withholding approval for a new BASF drug, Meridia. BASF was down 50 pfennigs at 47.60 marks.
